Playbook.name: Windows — Execution of an Unsigned Service - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A service binary's trustworthiness is in question. The original detection keyed on process.code_signature (NOT collected in JCB). RECOVERED: Sysmon collects process.hash.sha256 and process.pe.company/product (verified live), and 4697/7045 give the service image path - together a strong trust assessment without the signature field.
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: An unsigned/untrusted service running as SYSTEM is a persistence and privilege mechanism.

LogSources.LogSource: Windows Security/System + Sysmon - logs-system.security-*, logs-system.system-*, logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Sysmon collects process.hash.sha256 (318k docs) and process.pe.company/product (verified live); process.code_signature is NOT collected. Service installs in 4697/7045.

Signal.Name: Execution of an Unsigned Service
Signal.Details: Service binary trust assessed via hash + PE publisher (code_signature not collected).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether a service binary is trustworthy using hash reputation + PE publisher metadata + image path, since code_signature is not collected.

Step.name: Service installs and their binaries on the host
Step.Purpose: 4697/7045 give the service name and image path - the binary to assess.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-*,logs-system.system-* | WHERE event.code IN ("4697","7045") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, event.code, winlog.event_data.ServiceName, winlog.event_data.ServiceFileName, winlog.event_data.ImagePath | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A service image in temp/appdata/user-writable path is suspicious. Take the image path to INV-02 for hash + publisher.

Step.name: Hash + PE publisher for services.exe child binaries (trust evidence)
Step.Purpose: process.hash.sha256 (for reputation lookup) and process.pe.company/product (publisher legitimacy) replace the missing signature field.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* | WHERE event.code == "1" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.parent.name == "services.exe" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.executable, process.hash.sha256, process.pe.company, process.pe.product, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A service binary with a KNOWN publisher (process.pe.company e.g. Microsoft/Veritas) is likely legitimate. NO/blank company + a temp path + an unknown hash = likely unsigned malware. Look up process.hash.sha256 in threat intel/VirusTotal for the verdict. This is the trust assessment the code_signature field would have given.

Node.Condition: A services.exe child binary with no PE publisher, a temp/user path, and an unknown/malicious hash reputation.
A service binary with a known legitimate PE publisher and good hash reputation.
A legitimately-unsigned in-house tool with a known hash but no publisher.
Trust indeterminate from telemetry (no PE company, hash reputation unknown) - verify signature on host.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-SVC-INSTALL, INV-02-SVC-TRUST to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A legitimate service (known publisher / good hash).

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the software; close as false_positive.
Stop/remove the service; isolate the host; open IR.
Document the exception; consider signing the binary.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Assess the service binary via hash reputation + PE publisher + image path.
If untrusted, stop/remove the service and isolate.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Stop/remove the service; isolate the host; hunt the hash.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enable Sysmon ProcessCreate signature fields for direct signature verdicts; meanwhile hash+PE publisher is the working substitute; consider redesigning the detection to key on PE-publisher-absence + suspicious path.

QualityChecks.Check: RECOVERED: hash+PE publisher replace the uncollected code_signature for the trust assessment. The paired new_terms detection (on code_signature) cannot fire; redesign it to key on process.pe.company absence + services.exe parent + non-standard path.
Hash reputation lookup is an analyst step (external), not in-SIEM.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Malicious service removed; hash hunted; host contained.
